name: SealGate Management API
description:
The SealGate Management API is the REST control plane for the SealGate agentic-AI security gateway and data firewall. It lets security, IT, and compliance teams manage MCP servers, sessions, access-control roles, deterministic policy rules, approvals, agents, API keys, and observability data programmatically.

## Authentication
All endpoints require an HTTP Bearer credential: send `Authorization: Bearer <your-sealgate-api-key>`, where the token is a SealGate API key (obtained from the SealGate dashboard). This management API key is distinct from the MCP gateway credentials used by AI clients. Requests without a valid, active key receive `401`. A key whose role lacks the required permission receives `403`.

## Versioning and deprecation policy
The API is versioned in the URL path: every operation lives under `/api/v1`. Breaking changes (removing a field, changing a type, removing an endpoint) are shipped only under a new path prefix such as `/api/v2`; additive changes (new endpoints, new optional fields) are made in place under `/api/v1`. When an endpoint or field is scheduled for removal it is first marked `deprecated: true` in this specification and announced in the changelog at https://docs.sealgate.ai; deprecated surfaces continue to function for a published sunset window before a new major version drops them.

## Error model
Errors use standard HTTP status codes with a JSON body. Application errors raised by the API return `{"detail": {"error": <human-readable message>, "code": <machine-readable code>, "details": <object or null>}}`. Request-validation failures return `422` with `{"detail": [{"loc": [...], "msg": "...", "type": "..."}]}`. Every non-2xx response documents a typed JSON schema.

## Pagination
List endpoints are page-based. Pass `page` (1-indexed) and `per_page` query parameters; responses return an envelope with `items`, `total`, `page`, `per_page`, and `total_pages`.
